references.text: The first time it is mentioned that people called on the name of the Lord, as Abraham does here in Be'er-Sheva.
Abraham builds an altar and calls on the name of the Lord for the first time, a practice he continues in Be'er-Sheva.
Isaac builds an altar and calls on the name of the Lord in Be'er-Sheva, just as Abraham did.
Moses builds an altar and gives it a name that honors God, in line with Abraham's tradition of calling on the name of the Lord.
Refers to God as 'the eternal God' (Elohei qedem), a close parallel to the title 'El Olam' (God of Eternity) used by Abraham.
Explicitly uses the title 'eternal God' (El Olam) for the LORD, the most direct parallel to Abraham's invocation in Be'er-Sheva.
Expresses God's eternity 'from everlasting to everlasting you are God', reflecting Abraham's address of God as 'God of Eternity' (El Olam).
